summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 125.3% YoY to Rs 13,457 mn; EBITDA margin 18.9%, normalized PAT Rs 1,652 mn after Bawal fire exceptional loss of Rs 1,436 mn.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 125.3% YoY to Rs 13,457 mn and EBITDA rose 140.6% to Rs 2,548 mn, with margin up to 18.9% from 17.7%. A Rs 1,436 mn provisional exceptional loss from the Bawal facility fire brought reported PAT to Rs 578 mn (4.3% margin), while normalized PAT was Rs 1,652 mn (12.3%). Management raised full-year revenue growth guidance to about 70% from 50%, kept the margin guidance at "sustainable to improve," and added distributors, dealers and two states. Ratlam capacity additions (2 GW solar panel, 2 GW power electronics, 2 GW battery due Q2 FY27) and stake increases in Zayo entities were the main capex and integration moves.

financial_highlights.change: expected to be fully recovered via insurance

financial_highlights.metric: Normalized PAT (ex post-tax fire provision Rs 1,074 mn)

segments.name: Residential rooftop / B2C
segments.commentary: Management said about 90% of revenue comes from the B2C channel. Sales are sold as a package of panels, inverters and batteries; no segment-wise revenue split was given.

segments.name: Off-grid vs on-grid vs hybrid
segments.commentary: Management said on-grid growth was the main driver this quarter, enabled by in-house DCR cells; off-grid is still growing but more slowly. No split was disclosed.

segments.name: Tubular batteries
segments.commentary: Tubular battery output (about 10% of revenue) was lost in the Bawal fire; management estimated the gross margin impact at below 0.5% as batteries are now bought from outside vendors.

guidance_outlook: Full-year revenue growth guidance raised to about 70% from the earlier 50%, with a stated intent to trail it upward in later quarters.
EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 'sustainable to improve' (Q1 at 18.9%).
Insurance claim on the Bawal fire (net carrying value about Rs 1,436 mn) expected to settle by end of FY27; management expects full recovery.
Ratlam 2 GW lithium-ion battery plant on track for commissioning by Q2 FY27.
FY27 gross block (incl. CWIP) expected at about Rs 1,300 cr, up from about Rs 800 cr at start of year.
Channel partner target of more than 15,000 (distributors, dealers, shoppes) by end FY28.
Zayo Energy plant expected to add Rs 400-500 cr top-line in the next financial year; Fujiyama's share of Zayo capex about Rs 50 cr.
capex_capacity: Solar panel capacity: 2 GW added at Ratlam (capitalized 14 May 2026), taking total to 3.5 GW; Ratlam running one shift and ramping in phases.
Power electronics: 2 GW facility at Ratlam commissioned in August 2026, taking total to 4 GW; initial utilization of Ratlam capacity guided at 40-50%.
Solar cell (DCR) plant at 1 GW (some reports say 1.2 GW) running at 80%+ utilization; non-Ratlam panel plants at 70-80% utilization.
TOPCon line: building complete and machine orders placed; target commissioning in about 9 months (within the next financial year per the call).
Zayo Energy/Zayo Cables: stake raised from 19% to 50% each; Zayo Energy capex about Rs 180-200 cr total, with land acquisition under way and production targeted within about one year.
demand_pricing: Management cited current PM Surya Ghar installation run rate of about 1 GW per month; about 50 lakh of the 1 crore household target covered.
Industry rooftop capacity installed to date put at over 30 GW, with about 15 GW under PM Surya Ghar; government target 90-100 GW rooftop of 300 GW solar by 2030.
System pricing quoted at Rs 26-30 per watt (BOM with panel, inverter, battery) at distributor billing level, including GST.
Industry growth rate cited at about 40%; Fujiyama estimates about 10% share of the on-grid market (not officially confirmed).
Distributors rose from 950+ to 1,150+ in the quarter; channel partners rose from about 8,900 to over 10,100 with Odisha and Uttarakhand newly moved to covered states.
Management said DCR pricing and higher realization on Mono PERC DCR panels drove the higher average realization.

qa_highlights.question: How should full-year revenue and profit be modelled after a strong Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to about 70% from 50%, citing demand and Ratlam capacity, and said it will trail the guidance upward as the year progresses.

qa_highlights.question: Will backward integration lift margins or be passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DCR cell capacity supports margins but raw material price volatility is a factor, and it will pass on part of the gains; margin guidance remains 'sustainable to improve'.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Bawal fire loss is recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the damaged assets with net carrying value about Rs 143 cr are fully insured, the survey is done, the full loss was booked in Q1, and claim settlement is expected by year end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs 26-30 per watt figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an average distributor BOM (roughly Rs 15 panel, Rs 5 inverter, Rs 5 battery), varying with DCR/non-DCR, battery type and system type, with GST included.

qa_highlights.question: Capex funding for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no equity dilution this year; about Rs 200 cr of the Rs 500 cr additional capex will be debt-funded, with Rs 100 cr from IPO proceeds and Rs 200 cr from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the TOPCon line and the lead-acid plant after the fire?
qa_highlights.answer: TOPCon commissioning is targeted within about 9 months. The fire-hit lead-acid plant will not restart until insurance work is done; the company is in talks to lease an operating plant.

risks_watch: Bawal insurance claim settlement (management targets end FY27); any delay or shortfall versus Rs 1,436 mn would hit reported earnings.
Margin sustainability as market share is pushed with price cuts and as module prices fall; non-DCR margins are under pressure.
PM Surya Ghar 2.0 is not yet notified; loan sanction and DCR supply constraints are slowing installations.
Ratlam battery plant (2 GW) commissioning in Q2 FY27 and new power electronics ramp-up at 40-50% utilization.
BIS compliance: 15 of about 500 SKUs were flagged by the authority; management says these are now certified and represent under 1% of stock value.
Revenue is not disclosed by segment, which limits visibility into on-grid, off-grid and hybrid mix.
Zayo Energy stake commitments and capex (Rs 180-200 cr total) plus the lead-acid plant lease.
key_quotes: So, we would like to revise our guidance for the full year to 70% considering the robust demand which is there and the capacities that we are ready with in Ratlam.

But we'd also like to discount the fact that there are a lot of variable factors in the market in terms of raw material pricing and you have already covered our point that we will be passing on whatever margin gain that we will be gaining.
Now, if we provide it segment-wise, it leads to a lot of confusion.
Sir, we are adequately covered. We have taken considering the carrying value of the asset that got impacted, it is close to Rs. 143 crores and we are sufficiently covered under that.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and capacity: management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to about 70% and repeatedly stressed robust demand. Cautious on margins, keeping the "sustainable to improve" wording and citing raw material price volatility; evasive on segment revenue split, declining to quantify on-grid, off-grid and hybrid mix, and on the Zayo margin impact.
